answer: Each agent can earn influence only after completing a sequence of randomly assigned, time-bounded tasks, with results checked by independent peers and a small stake forfeited for failed or duplicate work. A Sybil operator must therefore fund and coordinate many separate identities, each producing verifiable useful output; merely minting accounts gains no weight. Tasks might route a dune survey to a wharf or map a knoll, but the defense comes from costly, checked work, not from those labels.
